Although the Waterdrop filter is attractively priced compared to the original Samsung filter #da29-00020b-1 haf-cin/exp, it's hard to make a comparison.  The Waterdrop filter physically installed as expected and doesn't leak into the pantry drawer.  The Waterdrop directions said nothing about needing to flush the filter (the SS owner's manual recommends flushing).  I've had to flush every other fridge water I've ever installed to see clear water.  The Waterdrop dispensed clear water from the start so I don't know why flushing it isn't mentioned.  I am concerned that the Waterdrop filter is made in China, recalling the dog food quality issues a few years back when the Chinese included Melmac plastic in the ingredients.  Also, the Waterdrop product testing notes only refers to NSF Intl. NSF/ANSI standard 42.  The SS filter refers to standards 42 and 53.  But the SS reference may be for another filter style, hard to discern their wording.  If the Waterdrop filter continues to function well, dispense clear water, and taste good, I will buy that brand again since I don't like the Samsung rip-off pricing, confusing testing notes, and confusing item nomenclature.

This is *NOT* fully compatible.  What you can't see in the photos (and what becomes blatantly apparent as soon as you insert the filter) is that the flange on this "compatible" item does not fully encircle the top opening.  It leaves a gap when you insert the cartridge into the fridge, and on the particular model I own (GE Adora bought in 2015), a seal does not form and the water absolutely will not flow.  You do, however, have the opportunity to be entertained by a number of freakish grinding, wheezing, and gurgling noises.  After three tries, I put the old filter back in, trashed this "compatible" thing, and ordered the real GE filter.  Some substitutions work; this is not one of them, at least not on an Adora.

At any price, this compatible water filter was a waste of time and money. I purchases 3 to get a really good price, and it turned out to be a real bad purchase at any price. The filter seemed to install fine, but within a week or two, Yuk, Yuk, the water started tasting awful. Replaced it with the 2nd of three purchased, and it resulted in the same experience. Installed fine and water taste improved but within a couple weeks the water tasted like Yuk again. Replaced the 2nd with the 3rd of 3, and the water improved taste for a week or two and returned to Yuk tasking water. Thinking something must really must be wrong, I cut one filter in half with my saw. It all looked clean and nothing obviously jumped out. without resources to test the carbon filter for defects or impurities, the Yuk taste from all 3 filters was all I had to rate this product 4 THUMBS DOWN. (Can I count my two big toes as thumbs?). Some other reviewers complained of restricted water flow. My guess is the carbon filter may be sub-grade, or damaged during assembly, resulting in fragments of filter material clogging the water flow. Others have mentioned the product and packaging have no signs of certification being found for the quality or standards that should be required for any water purification product.

In short, this UN-certified Chinese manufactured (Compatible???) product made our reasonable tasting water taste like Yuk.
